experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r2-prefix-v1 target. One run of steps S1 to S3 of proof.md Section 4 per organizer seed, each returning a 60-byte message and a 62-byte message. Nine state words are taken from the seed. Every trial is returned. The program does not call a hash; the organizer recomputes both digests.
experiments.hypothesis: For every trial the two complete 2-round digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, that is on the 128 masked bits, as the theorem of proof.md Section 5 states for every choice of the nine state words. This is an exact claim; the run checks it on concrete inputs.

experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r2-prefix-v1 target. The search of proof.md Section 6 at toy scale: per organizer seed one context and one alpha, then at most 8192 consecutive gamma values, stopping at the first trial whose residual has a zero low byte in digest word 1. Failed trials are returned as null pairs.
experiments.hypothesis: Every returned pair agrees on 136 digest bits: the 128 bits of the half-collision and the low byte of digest word 1. Under heuristic H1 a trial has this extra byte zero with probability near 2^-8 or above, so nearly all seeds return a pair within 8192 values. This is small-scale evidence about the residual; it does not measure the 128-bit hit rate and is not evidence of attack cost.
